utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution winding up cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You remember yesterday Mr. Antic I took you through a few basic propositions towards the end of the examination yesterday. You recall that evidence that you gave?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And I produced to you -- sought to produce to you Exhibit P164. MR. DI FAZIO: And I wonder if that might be produced to the witness again, please, the B/C/S version, with ter, I suppose. I wonder, if Ms. Usher, if we could open the document, place it on the ELMO at paragraph 11. Now, I just remind you that, again, that I asked you about certain events towards the end of my cross-examination concerning what transpired in Bosanski Samac, the events that you saw unfolding there around April of 1992. Now, please have a look at paragraph 11. You can see it there on the ELMO. Just read it.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You see that it says, "In October of 1991 and the months following the SDS intensified efforts to ensure that the objective of ethnic separation by force would be achieved in the event that a negotiated solution did not occur." Do you see that? "These steps included arming large segments of the Bosnian population in collaboration with among others the JNA, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the MUP of Serbia and Serbian paramilitaries, establishing Serbian military and police formations and coordinating with the JNA and paramilitary units from within and outside Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Biljana Plavsic pleaded guilty to, accepted as being the factual basis of her plea of guilty. That's in fact what was occurring in Bosanski Samac, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These things in Bosanski Samac did not enjoy support in the attempts by the Yugoslav People's Army to prevent interethnic conflicts in Bosanski Samac. So I personally believe that this is a personal act, personal admission on the part of Mrs. Plavsic, but as a commander, I state that these efforts, as it is stated here, did not have any connection, because the command of the Tactical Group, of the 17th Tactical Group, did not order or convey anything to this effect to the command of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You see the reference in paragraph 11 of this document that I've directed your attention to, the reference to "the arming of large segments of the Bosnian Serb population in collaboration with, among others, the JNA, the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the MUP of Serbia and Serbian paramilitaries and the establishment of Serbian military and police formations, and coordinating with the JNA and paramilitary units from within and outside Bosnia and Herzegovina." Specifically, those matters were occurring in Bosanski Samac, were they not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of these things did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P127. And please, if we just retain the P164 there as well. Thanks, Ms. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, again, if we put it on the ELMO so everyone can see. The paragraph that I'm interested in is the -- I suppose it's in effect the second paragraph, and you should be able to read it. And it says -- do you see the paragraph beginning with the words "First it is a fact that TG 17, Tactical Group 17 command played a significant role in the pre-war period." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. I'll just read it out very briefly: "First it is a fact that the Tactical Group 17 command played a significant role in the pre-war, pre-war period, and even in the first days of the war in the military and territorial organisation of several detachments in Samac municipality. The organised arming of the Serbian people in particular, and the provision of proper combat tactics and equipment for the armed struggle in this region." Did you see that phenomenon taking place in Bosanski Samac, the JNA and Tactical Group 17 involving itself in the organised arming of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th Tactical Group informing these detachments and through the appropriate regulations of the JNA and informing these units, armed its members, and in the specific case of the 4th Detachment, armed members of the 4th Detachment who were actually members of all three ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So you can't -- is it your position that you don't know what the document is talking about when it says that Tactical Group 17 played a significant role in the arming of the Serbian people pre-war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I understood this process through the forming of specifically the 4th Detachment and the setting out of its functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Have a look at paragraph 12 of P164. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Ms. Usher. I've finished with P127.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Paragraph 12. I'll just briefly read it out, and perhaps if you follow it in the B/C/S: "In addition, the SDS prepared and distributed written instructions to SDS municipal leaders to form crisis staffs, proclaim Serbian Municipal Assemblies and carry out preparations for the formation of municipal governmental bodies and to mobilise Bosnian Serb police, Territorial Defence forces, and subordinate them to JNA command. The municipal crisis staffs implemented these objectives and directives in the field, including ultimately the objective of ethnic separation by force." Now, that is what Biljana Plavsic pleaded guilty to as part of the factual basis of her plea of guilty. Those same events took place on the ground in Bosanski Samac, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of these facts from this paragraph, as they are defined there, did take place in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, but I also state that such instructions or written instructions, as it is stated here, was something that the 4th Detachment did not receive from anybody. So in that sense did not receive any specific tasks, neither from the political parties nor from the command of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, maybe you're going to do this, but just in case you're not: Mr. Antic said some of the facts as defined there did take place. I wonder whether, Mr. Antic, we could find out from you which of those facts did take place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The facts are that crisis staffs were formed, that organs of authority were established, that police forces were mobilised, and so on. But all of this didn't have any effect on the command of the JNA, nor did the commands of the JNA or my superiors able to have any influence in these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. The factual basis indicates that the SDS and Serb leaders and the JNA coordinated efforts. You weren't present, were you, at any high-level meetings between the JNA and SDS and Serb leaders, with Karadzic and Plavsic, those people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I never attended any kinds of accords at the highest levels or at the lowest levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about any agreements they made?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: However, it is a fact, isn't it, that the 4th Detachment was not ordered to retake the town, reinstall the elected government, or remove the Serb Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No such orders were given to the 4th Detachment. Only those orders were issued which I talked about and which the 4th Detachment carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And that fact is consistent with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That fact is consistent with an agreement between the JNA and the Serb leaders in Bosanski Samac, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. The witness already said that he was not aware of this agreement, if ever existed such an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Very well. Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination of the witness. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a couple of questions regarding Crisis Staff questions, since my client was for a brief period a member of the Crisis Staff, so I would like to clarify that, some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antic, the Prosecutor, during the cross-examination, asked you about the role of the Crisis Staff in the arrest and the expulsion or persecution campaign, and I would like to focus on some answers that you gave him. I would like some clarifications in relation to that. First, the Prosecutor asked you whether you agree that immediately after the 16th and the 17th of April, a large number of non-Serbs were arrested. Do you remember that the Prosecutor asked you that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: Who arrested those people in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police and the volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you whether you were familiar with the fact that a number of detentions were formed in Bosanski Samac in the SUP, in the TO building, in the gym of the high school. Could you please tell us: Who secured those detentions? Who were the guards?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I knew that there were four of such prisons in Bosanski Samac. I also know that those prisons were secured by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you about a number of Croat citizens who were taken to Crkvina. Do you know who took those people to Crkvina and who guarded them?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the following, and I've said that: A number of Croatians, Croat citizens, were arrested in Crkvina, and this was carried out by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also suggested that in the activities of arrest and these other things, the Crisis Staff also took part, so I would like to ask you: Did you ever attend any meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the Prosecutor only what my opinion was. I never attended a meeting of the Crisis Staff. I never personally spoke with any member of the Crisis Staff either. And I also state that I never had in my hands any document by the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, and finally, does that mean that you don't have any immediate knowledge about the role of the Crisis Staff in the arrests and the persecution campaign?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally do not have any direct knowledge or proof of that. I just stated my assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antic. I don't have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Antic. As far as I understood from your answers to my learned friend Mr. Krgovic, what you said to the Prosecutor yesterday in response to the question that there were less than 50 per cent of Serbs in the territory of the Samac municipality, and regarding the arrest of non-Serbs their interrogations, mistreatment, and so on, and also about the alleged role of the Crisis Staff. So this whole series of questions which the Prosecutor asked. And so as not to repeat each of these questions. We're talking about your assumptions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Particularly the last question which I interpreted just now, that is my assumption. Everything else are just well-known facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, Mr. Antic, and explain to the Trial Chamber, in relation to the territory of the Samac municipality before the war, before 1992, which included Prud, Domaljevac, and so on, that was the territory of the municipality prior to the war. Now, please tell me: From the 16th or the 17th of April, 1992, until today, how was the municipality of Samac formed? Did it remain in the same borders as before the 17th of April or -- MR. DI FAZIO: [Previous interpretation continues] ... municipality from April of 1992 didn't arise in my cross-examination at all, plus that its continued life up to the present day is not a matter of relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, because the first question of my learned friend was whether the population -- Serb population in the municipality of Samac was less than 50 per cent. So I would like to establish now and to see with this witness in fact on which part this answer was related. Because we know that the -- I don't want to suggest any -- MR. DI FAZIO: We know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I just wanted to say that if I recall correctly, my question in cross-examination was reasonably precise. I asked about the population as at April of 1992. That was the aspect of demographics that I touched upon and that's what arose in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now I have to clarify that, on which exact territory this witness meant. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is the situation with the territory of the municipality, et cetera. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. Perhaps I misunderstood. If that's the only issue that Mr. Pantelic is going to, then I'll withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. If I understood the questions by the Prosecution correctly, he asked about the portions of different ethnicities in the town of Bosanski Samac, not the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact, I was related to the basis of the question of my learned friend from the Prosecution. It's page 71 of the LiveNote version of yesterday's transcript. And his question was: "Before the 17th of April, Serbs were less than 50 per cent of the municipality of Bosanski Samac; correct?" That was the question. So it was related to the municipality, in fact, not town. Town is a part of the municipality. MR. DI FAZIO: I think, if Your Honours please, Mr. Pantelic is correct on that, but that's the only issue that I raised as far as demographics is concerned. Now, if it's to clarify that, no objection, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, let me repeat: From the 17th of April onwards, did the municipality of Samac remain in the same integral borders as before? Could you please explain this to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Compared to the pre-war structure, the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, I can say that before the war, the territory of Bosanski Samac included the village of Prud, included the Croatian village of Bazik, the Croatian village of Domaljevac, the Croatian village of Grebnice. The ethnic structure of the population at the time in the Samac municipality was 43.3 per cent Serbs, 43.7 Croats, 6 per cent Muslims, 7 per cent Yugoslavs, and as far as I can remember, under 3 per cent of others, which means that in the pre-war period, none of the ethnic groups had more than 50 per cent in the structure. All of them were represented under 50 per cent in terms of population. After the events of the 17th of April, the Bosanski Samac municipality no longer included the Croat village of Prud, the Croat village of Bazik, the Croat village of Domaljevac, and a large part of the Croat village of Grebnice. Only a small part of the Croat village of Grebnice --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was part of the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, can you tell me now, since the Prosecutor asked you about the local municipal government that were elected in the multiparty 1990 elections, there were questions in relation to this: Do you have any personal knowledge and can you tell the Trial Chamber, from the 17th of April, 1992, in this territory that you've just mentioned, that is, Domaljevac, et cetera, was there a municipality, some organ that was formed there? Do you have any personal knowledge, some authority? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Croatian village of Prud was included in the municipality of Odzak, and in the territory of these villages that I've mentioned, what was in operation was the municipality of Domaljevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is that Samac Domaljevac or is it just Domaljevac? What's the difference? Do you know, by any chance? If you don't, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the accurate information about that, what it is called today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me: From the 17th of April, 1992, do you know, do you have any personal knowledge, in this territory around Domaljevac, who was the one who established authority? Who was in charge in that territory as from 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there an organ, a body, that was established there, and if it was, were there any Serbs that were members of it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never or I have never been there until now, in that territory. As far as I know, what was established there was Croatian authority, and the Serbs did not participate in that organ of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me: Yesterday, on a couple of occasions, you explained something, and I want to clarify this. The Prosecutor asked you on a couple of occasions some questions, where there was a suggestion that these volunteers were heavily armed. However, in one of your answers, you said they only had light weapons. In order to avoid any misunderstanding, when we're analysing this part of the transcript, could you please tell the Trial Chamber: How were these volunteers armed? Were they heavily armed or lightly armed? Could you please expand.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the questions asked by the Prosecutor on several occasions, what was mentioned is that Serb volunteers, volunteers from Serbia were heavily armed. In each of my answers -- I couldn't correct the Prosecutor, but in each of my answers, there is in fact included that they had light infantry weapons, light firearms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. I was just wanting to have maybe just a little brief elaboration of what you actually mean by "light firearms." Would you be specific? Was it Kalashnikovs? Was it semi-automatics, what have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terms of light firearms, what I mean, the personal weapons were all kinds of handguns, then automatic rifles, then light machine-gun. Also, when I say "a light firearms," light infantry weapons, it's also a hand-held rocket launcher which is used for anti-tank combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine. Thank you very much, Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further on, on page 49 on yesterday's transcript, the Prosecutor asked you whether you agreed that those who brought those volunteers from Serbia, that that included the Crisis Staff as well, and you said yes. Is that -- is your answer based on a specific fact or is this your opinion and your assumption that Crisis Staff as a body was also included in the arrival of the volunteers? Could you please expand on that and clarify.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a piece of information at my disposal that these volunteers were brought by Stevan Todorovic, but if there is a connection between Stevan Todorovic and the Crisis Staff, then that is an entirely different matter that I know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antic. Further on, on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I'm not sure that I understand your answer, that if there's a connection between Stevan Todorovic and the Crisis Staff, that's an entirely different matter. I wonder whether you could maybe just elaborate a little bit, just to make clear what you mean about the Crisis Staff, based on what you said yesterday. Because this now seems a little bit uncertain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can clarify. Since I know for certain that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff, but whether the arrival of the volunteers he had been given instructions by the Crisis Staff. I do know that there was a connection, because he was a member of the Crisis Staff. However, whether he had been issued an order, I have nothing to base this upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In relation to this, Mr. Antic, now that you have mentioned this, how do you know that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff? Can you please explain the basis for your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a well-known fact, and also --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. You personally -- I'm sorry to interrupt you, but was there any kind of official announcement, information? Did you hear this from him? What was the basis for your personal knowledge that he was a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based this upon that he was a member of the Crisis Staff was his post, his function, that he was at the municipality of Bosanski Samac. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it may be that the witness has covered what I'm about to express some concern about. Mr. Pantelic asked him the basis of the knowledge. He said this is a well-known fact and also -- he started to give an answer. Now, it may be that he was just going to go on to explain the fact that membership led him to that conclusion. If so, there's no problem. But if he had something else in mind, then he should be permitted to finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness should be -- should complete the answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said: Based upon my knowledge of the structure of the authorities, he was a member of the Crisis Staff, on the basis of the function that he had in the municipality, which was that he was the police chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So what you mean is that on the basis of your pre-war knowledge, you draw this conclusion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I draw this conclusion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you cannot state with 100 per cent certainty that since 17th of April, 1992 it was the same as before the war. What is the level -- the degree of your certainty? That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I think the witness has answered sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell me: On page 47, when you answered the Prosecutor, in relation to the orders regarding certain events, there were certain things that remained unexplained. You were asked what were these decisions based upon the Crisis Staff decisions, and you said that knowing the structure of the authority, the orders in relation to certain events were issued by the Crisis Staff, and organs of the interior, and these organs would be implementing the Crisis Staff orders, specifically. Considering that you've explained the MUP structure, how it was organised according to the hierarchy, in relation to this answer I'd like you to clarify whether the Crisis Staff in any way was able to issue orders to the organs of the interior, that is, to the police in Samac, organisationally speaking, to the Ministry of the Interior. That's what I'd like to know, since you had been a chief of police before.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This structure of authority in peacetime I am very familiar with it, because I have been in Samac as head of the police, and this police was organised according to the vertical chain of command. But I also know that the organ of internal affairs was answerable to the Assembly and would report about its work to the Assembly, about each year that passed. So the only thing that I can do is assume that the organ of internal affairs, in a similar -- through a similar hierarchy, was answerable, that is, it was able to, according to that chain, carry out certain tasks that they were given through the vertical chain of command. But my assumption is that it was the organ, that is, the police, at least in some way was connected to the organ of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, on page 43 of yesterday's transcript, you were asked by the Prosecutor about Crisis Staff being established before the 16th or the 17th of April and that throughout that time it was Dr. Blagoje Simic who headed the Crisis Staff. Because this was a two-part question, and now what remains unclear: Your answer was, "Yes, I know about that." It remains unclear whether you know that Dr. Blagoje Simic was headed by that or whether you know that this body was formed before the 16th or the 17th. Because there was something else that you said that you knew about the Crisis Staff only about the declaration of the 18th of April. So in order to clarify this, I'd like to ask you something very specific. Do you know for sure that it was before the 17th of April, 1992, that the Crisis Staff was established? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, that's not strictly correct. My question was, and the wording is important: "You know this body, the Serbian municipalities of Bosanski Samac appointed a Crisis Staff just before the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. The Crisis Staff that was headed throughout its life by one of the defendants in this case, Blagoje Simic." So my question -- it's always been agreed in this case that it was headed by the -- the president was Blagoje Simic. It's an admitted fact in this case. There's no problem about that. So my question was simply whether the Serbian municipality appointed a Crisis Staff before the 16th and 17th. Answer: "Yes, I know about that." So just for the sake -- the question was precise. I wasn't asking him: Was it a Crisis Staff appointed before the 16th? And secondly, was the head of it Blagoje Simic? The question was simply to identify the Crisis Staff that I was talking about, the one headed by --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my point, Your Honour. This was a two-barreled question. So I want to clarify with this witness: What was his answer related to the notion that Mr. Blagoje Simic was -- because he is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the Prosecution has explained, and the question was quite clear. And as he says that there has never been any dispute as to who was the president of the Crisis Staff. That is also clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Since there is some ambiguity between the other question, I would like to clarify that with the witness, with the other answer that he said that first he knew about the existence of the Crisis Staff on the 18th of April, after the proclamation that he heard on the radio, so on. MR. DI FAZIO: Then it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is a -- you know -- MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. I do apologise. Then it's unnecessary, because the witness then went on to say: "Specifically I heard when the Crisis Staff was first heard of through its proclamation, and I think this was on the 18th." That's what he said about it. There's no uncertainty. That's what he thinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Anyhow, to clarify that finally, I will try to do that through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, in your asking -- when you're asking questions, do not ask the witness to repeat what has already been stated by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. Not my intention. Just his personal knowledge about the existence of certain body, simple as that, regarding to particular period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Antic, let's clarify this. When was it that you personally found out about the existence of the Crisis Staff of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an official context, my first -- the first time I found out about the existence of the Crisis Staff was at the moment when, at the command of the 17th Tactical Group, the Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic told me about the contents of what Dr. Blagoje Simic informed him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you had no official announcement, decision; this was just from your talk. That was the basis for your knowledge. That's how I understood.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my first official information that I had, because I assume that my commander had this fact, that is, that he knew about this fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And just for the sake of clarity: That meeting with Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic told you about this, that was on April 17th, 1992, at your early morning meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. At the command, at the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The following subject on page 41 of yesterday's transcript. When the Prosecutor suggested that the SDS was the moving force in relation to the establishment of certain institutions or organs, and you said that you knew about that. Further on, you said that on the session of the 28th of March of the Municipal Assembly in Obudovac, you don't know about any decisions that were taken there, you never read them, and so on. Now I'm asking you: In relation to the SDS, what other parties were involved in the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo that was being formed? Do you know anything about it, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never a member of the SDS, so I never looked into this. What was the structure of the political position of this party. My political conviction --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. I have to interrupt you. I think you didn't understand. You said that the SDS was this moving force which created the Municipal Assembly, the Serb Municipal Assembly. I'm asking you very simply whether at this Assembly there were deputies that belonged to some other parties. That's all I'm asking you. If you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this, because I did not participate in the structure of this authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Following question: Do you know whether the Crisis Staff, apart from the SDS, they were members of the other parties? If you know, please answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any other -- members of any other ethnic groups in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On page 30 of yesterday's transcript, the Prosecutor asked you about the volunteers and another topic which is very important to clarify here. You said in the military sense, they did not represent or constitute a significant number, in a military sense, for this territory which was in the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group. Could you please tell me, since you've already mentioned the weapons and now you say that in the military sense they didn't have any significant role: Mr. Antic, could you please tell me the following: Why do you, as commander of the 4th Detachment, why did you not, as commander of the 4th Detachment, arrest that insignificant group in the military sense, since you were a commander of a group of 450 armed soldiers? Why did you not arrest this small group that was looting and doing other things? Could you please tell me what your motive was.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that question. The 4th Detachment did not have the order to arrest anyone, because the 4th Detachment did not have any police forces as part of it which would be able to carry out such a task, nor did we receive any orders to that effect. I already said which orders the 4th Detachment received. If you're thinking of the period before the events, that is not in the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment. So the 4th Detachment was not able to do a thing in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please explain to the Court the role of the commander and his responsibilities, of a commander of a military unit. You are a reserve officer and a former chief of police, and you do have a certain amount of experience. Could you please tell me: Is it the role of the military commander to act in accordance with the situation or to wait for orders of the Superior Command and to take on all the risks in the terrain at the time? So could you please tell me that, you as an experienced soldier.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a commander, I was obliged to carry out orders, and that is what I did, in the sense of how that order was issued. I said I was not able to, under my responsibilities, undertake to arrest anyone, not even those who would shoot a member, for example, of the 4th Detachment in the back on the line of defence. This was a police matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One of the tasks of the 4th Detachment, as you said yourself, was to protect the people and the property in their area of responsibility. Mr. Antic, there is an experienced officer of the Finnish army here, and a judge of much experience, sitting in this courtroom, and this Trial Chamber has already had many such cases. You, as a former military commander, are now telling me that you didn't have any possibility of preventing this group of volunteers who were robbing and mistreating volunteers. You had no way of doing anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this question was pursued yesterday. He has explained how he was acting with the people under whose command -- who were under his command. I don't think we need to repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have just a couple more questions and I'm finished, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me: Did you submit a criminal report or any criminal charges against these people when you discovered that they were robbing and mistreating the citizens?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a question that you should put to the person who was responsible and who should have carried out the arrests of those people. This is not a question for the commander of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just tell me, Mr. Antic: Did you file criminal charges or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, I personally, during the time that I was performing the function of commander, nor the command itself, submitted or filed criminal charges against anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And lastly, could you please tell us, Mr. Antic: Why did you ask for safe conduct and guarantees that you would not be arrested when you were coming here to The Hague? What were you afraid of? What did you think?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, that is not a question for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I've finished. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Antic. I would like to ask several questions in order to clarify some of the answers you gave during the cross-examination by the Prosecution and also during cross-examination by the other colleagues. One of the questions put to you by the Prosecutor was the arrival of volunteers to the village of Batkusa on the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Since you had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the interpreters said they didn't catch the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was the 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Since you were in their immediate presence, could you please describe to us what the members of that volunteer group were wearing, what insignia did they wear, and so on. Could you provide some more details. Because there were questions here regarding the way they looked.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since I did see them, I think this was on the second day after they landed, I can say that they wore multicoloured uniforms, that they had knitted black caps on their heads, that a number of them carried hats, wore hats, of various shapes; that they had different colours painted on their faces; that they had some insignia on their clothing which were not the insignia of the Yugoslav People's Army. They had some emblems on their sleeves, patches with some symbols embroidered on them bearing some names that they had given to themselves, for example, the Eagles, Grey Wolves, and I don't know what other names they called themselves by.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this group ever was under the command of any unit of the Yugoslav People's Army before the 17th or the 16th and the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The group was not under the command of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it ever -- was that group ever placed under the command of any unit of the JNA after the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the events of the 17th of April, 1992, I was familiar with the fact that with the reorganisation of the army of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: We haven't gotten to the army of Republika Srpska yet. I'm only asking you now about the period when the Yugoslav People's Army existed in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were never under the command of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were they ever under the command of the 4th Detachment or under your command?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of them were ever under my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who commanded that volunteer group that had arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were under the command of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And one more question: How far is the village of Obudovac from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the village of Batkusa is 13 kilometres from Samac, and the next village after that is Obudovac, and that is something over 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I will ask you a couple of questions about the organisation of the 4th Detachment, since my colleague Pantelic asked about -- some questions about the reconnaissance unit and so on. You said that there were four companies, there were platoons, there were squads. So could you tell me: Which squads existed in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several squads as part of the 4th Detachment. For example, the communication squad, which had three members; the logistics squad, or the quartermaster's squad; the medical squad; and if there was any need, we would form also a reconnaissance squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And when did this squad become functional?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time we went to carry out our combat tasks, meaning when the 4th Detachment went to the defence -- line of defence, then the need arose to form a reconnaissance squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And was it formed then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber: Who was the commander of that reconnaissance squad?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the reconnaissance squad was Fadil Topcagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you remember, any other members of that reconnaissance squad?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the reconnaissance squad is a squad with quite specific tasks and is directly responsible to the command, I can remember some of its members. For example, Stanko Bojic, Jasmin Ibralic, Damir Ibralic, Aleksandar Bogdanovic, and I can remember a few others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were the tasks of that reconnaissance squad? What were they supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks of the reconnaissance squad begins to be implemented from the moment -- at a certain position is taken up, i.e. from the moment that the 4th Detachment is activated. The task of the reconnaissance squad is to reconnoitre and to monitor enemy positions, movements of its troops, the disposition of their war materiel, observe which positions is artillery fire coming from, so basically to collect all information of significance for the combat activity of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who does the commander of the reconnaissance squad submit his report to about all the things that he has observed regarding enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the reconnaissance squad directly reports to the commander about all the significant data they have gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing. The commander of the reconnaissance squad, what kind of a function is that? Is that an officer post? What would be the ranks that can be in that post?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be a commander in a squad is not a function; it's a soldier's duty, which can be given to any soldier that is believed to be capable of carrying out that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about some patrols of the 4th Detachment. I would like to clarify that situation? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just before Mr. Pisarevic moves to this new topic of patrols, there's just been a body of evidence about something called reconnaissance squads. I understood from the witness that these were formed when they first went to combat duties, and my assumption is that he's talking about the formation of reconnaissance squads after the 17th of April, 1992, but that's not absolutely clear. And with respect, I think you should be clear about that, were these reconnaissance squads formed after the 17th, and were they something different from the patrols that were operating in the town beforehand; otherwise, you may end up being confused as to whether he's talking about patrols or something quite distinct, namely, these reconnaissance squads that he's spoken of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness can explain that. Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You did understand?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: How many reconnaissance squads there were?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 4th Detachment, there was only one reconnaissance squad, which would be activated, as I said, according to need, and it had ten members. This reconnaissance squad has nothing to do with the patrols that the 4th Detachment would task with patrolling the town after certain events were reported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the other aspect was when it was first formed, the reconnaissance squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the witness did answer that, but I will ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us: When was the first time that this reconnaissance squad was formed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reconnaissance squad was established after the 4th Detachment became activated, which was after the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to the question of the patrols now. These patrols, do they have anything in connection to the reconnaissance squad?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing at all. They didn't even operate at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us: At what time were these patrols of the 4th Detachment operational, and until when?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The patrols were operational only until the 17th of April. Their very last activity was on the 17th of April, and they were established in the month of February. And I have said how the procedure went as to the establishment of the patrols of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude, then, that after the 17th of April, 1992, there were no more patrols of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: After the 17th of April, was it activated, the medical squad?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All of the squads then became active.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Who was the commander of the medical squad in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the medical squad in the 4th Detachment was Dr. Mirko Sisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You explained what the patrols did, what their tasks were, but now I'd like to ask you if you can explain: How were these patrols decided on? Who decided on them, their composition, and how was this done in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the command of the detachment, we agreed on the principles, on the basis of which patrols should be established. We decided that this would be five to six patrols in all, that the patrols should be mixed, of mixed composition, as I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But who decided on the composition, on the schedule of the patrols?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The composition of the patrols was decided on by the commanders of the platoons, in agreement with the commanders of the squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you in the command have any knowledge, could you have had any knowledge, which people would be members of certain patrols at any given night?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command did not decide on the composition of the patrols. This was decided on by the commanding officers of lower-echelon units. So we were just informed what the patrols observed during the night, what they uncovered, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which members of the 4th Detachment were in the patrols in the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that our first pieces of information regarding the events that occurred in Samac was the information that we received from the patrols. These patrols would come; that is, they came after they acquired the knowledge, they came to the command. The moment when I entered the command, that is, that would be about half past 3.00 on the 17th of April, some of the members of the patrols were already in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall one of or some of these members of the patrols that were already in the command, who were submitting the reports on what was happening in the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could remember some of them, and that was, for instance, Darko Misic, Vlado Sisic, Djordje Devrenic - I believe that is his name - and there were others, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you: Is it possible, could you recall that Stanko Dujkovic was also one of them?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that Ilija Serjanovic was one of them?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Considering the patrols that went to the command, was it with the help of your RUP 2 radio station? Was it possible to keep in contact with the patrols while they were patrolling the town? And what was the technical equipment of the patrols, if they had any technical equipment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since in the command we had this equipment at our disposal, it is with this equipment that we kept in contact with the command of the 17th Tactical Group. The members of the patrols did not have any communication means, because I presume the Yugoslav People's Army did not have these equipment at their disposal that they could have issued to the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So let us conclude. The command did not have any communication or possibility to contact the patrols that were in the town?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no communication equipment. We had none to contact the patrols, to be in communication with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: We'll go on to another subject now. This is to do with the questions that you were asked by my colleague Mr. Pantelic. He asked you about the arrival of the tanks to Bosanski Samac. Can you tell us: You said there were none, but can you tell us: What was the first time that the tanks arrived in the town of Bosanski Samac, and how many were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that it was in the afternoon hours in Samac, two tanks arrived. That was about, I believe, 2.00 or 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Which date? When was that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps mean two APCs on the 17th? I was asking you about the tanks.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know also about the APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When did they come, the APCs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they arrived on the 18th. That was the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, you do make a distinction between the APCs and the tanks.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What arrived first: The APCs or the tanks? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, Mr. Pisarevic is now venturing into cross-examination. He's trying to get an answer. This is re-examination. The witness is clear. The tanks arrived on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On the 17th. MR. DI FAZIO: The 17th, the APCs on the 18th. That's the end of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the witness has explained that he knows the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe you may. I don't know what you're going to say, but the Trial Chamber may allow you. I don't know what you will say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the witness can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to say that I may have well made a mix-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What mix-up?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the events occurred in such a way that these APCs were not -- these vehicles were not placed under my command. I didn't ask for these vehicles, but this was probably, probably, that is, I assume that this was the command of the 17th Tactical Group had established and assessed that the 4th Detachment should be assisted, considering that the 4th Detachment only had firearms, and it was already from the 17th that we were under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What was the mix-up?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've mixed up the order of the arrival of these vehicles. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the witness has just said that these military vehicles, he assumes, were under the command of the 17th Tactical Group and that they were there to assist the 4th Detachment. You may care to know in what capacity armoured vehicles were assisting the 4th Detachment, because the witness has testified over the last two few days of two orders, securing lines and disarming the population, and you may care to know whether armoured vehicles were of use to the 4th Detachment in the peaceful collection of weapons or the securing of the lines. And so I invite you to seek clarification of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has understood what the Prosecutor has said, and the witness can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, of course the witness will explain. But I'd like to say that the witness has already said that the 4th Detachment, that is, on the 17th, in the evening, it was already under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: However, could you explain: How was it that two APCs came on the 17th and the tanks arrived on the 18th? Could you please expand on that. What was the situation? Were there any attacks, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the takeover --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- taking the defence line on the embankments of the Sava River, I understood in my own mind that what most probably happened was that the expected attacks would be -- that is, I allowed myself to believe that the 17th Tactical Group command had better intelligence than I did at the time. I also said that when we took up the positions, one of our members was seriously injured. I had already had my baptism of fire, as the soldiers call it. I had already had casualties. So I understood how serious the entire situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was there an attack on the town of Bosanski Samac, that is, on the lines that you took the members of the 4th Detachment to?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already on the 17th of April, in the morning of that day, that the town and the detachment was subjected to mortar attack from the Republic of Croatia, and it was on the 18th, in the morning of that day, that followed the attack from the direction of the village of Prud, across the bridge of the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What units launched this attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This attack was launched by the HVO units that had their positions in the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say "HVO," you mean the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the HVO unit. HVO is the abbreviation that we use for the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Whose army is this? Whose unit is this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the army, that is, the troops of the Croatian community of Bosnian Posavina [Realtime transcript read in error "Bosnia and"].

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, that is not the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the army of the Croatian defence council, that is, of the Croatian community in the area of Bosnia and Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And how did this attack end?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This attack ended in such a way that it was from the defence line that the 4th Detachment opened fire, from light infantry weapons, and I saw with my binoculars that several people remained dead on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... transcript. On page 35, line 12. Of Bosnian Posavina, not Bosnia and Posavina. This is the correct word for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What, you said Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Bosnian Posavina. That's what we use to -- these are the words that we used during proceedings for Bosnian Posavina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, is this a good time for a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When those tanks that we talked about came to Bosanski Samac, came into the town, where were they located?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the tanks was located on the line of defence towards the bridge over the Bosna River. The other tank was positioned at the crossroads near the so-called Uzarija.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were these tanks under your command?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks had their own crew, and they were under the command of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You talked a lot here about your responsibilities as a commander, about the system of subordination, unity of command, singleness of command, and so on. I wanted to ask you one question about that. Had Commander Nikolic, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, ordered you, as the commander of the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army, to take the town of Samac, would you have carried out that order or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an officer of the Yugoslav People's Army, and as a responsible man, I would carry out that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Just for the sake of clarity, at least in the English translation, it says: "If you had been ordered to take the town of Samac." That sounds as though he would be ordered to be the aggressor. Do you mean to protect, to take back, rather than take, in the initial instance? So in terms of your question, there's the lack of clarity, not the answer. Obviously, Mr. Antic understood what you meant, but for the record, I think if you could just be a bit more precise there or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Had you been ordered to place under control the town of Samac, by using the 4th Detachment, in order to secure and carry out the task of preventing the spillover of the war from Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina, would you have carried out that order?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I would carry out that order, as a responsible officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. As a follow-up question: When you met, in the early morning of the 17th of April, 1992, with Stevan Nikolic, if he had ordered you to take back or recover the town of Bosanski Samac, would you have followed that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any order that the commander would issue, I would carry out, but not an order which could be treated in a different way i.e. would be contrary to some other laws.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. I think we need a built of clarity on what that answer meant. MR. DI FAZIO: I was going to seek clarity to His Honour's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. Because I -- Mr. Antic, you say: "Any order that the commander would issue, I would carry out, but not an order which could be treated in a different way, would be contrary to some other laws." Do you mean international humanitarian law, Geneva Conventions, or do you mean municipal laws or laws of Republika Srpska? I mean, could you tell us what exactly you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think -- I'm thinking of those laws which would relate to the jeopardy for the lives of people, i.e. the carrying out of certain criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but he still hasn't answered Judge Lindholm's question. Would he obey the order to retake the town apparently from the paramilitaries, the Serb Crisis Staff and the Serbian police that have taken over the town if he was ordered to do so from the JNA command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Now that is specific. The question is now specific and the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer Judge Lindholm's question. Could you tell us briefly whether you would carry out that order or not.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: A little earlier you responded to a question that I was actually going to put to you, and that was the question: In which situation can a soldier refuse, or an officer, an order by his superior? Could you please tell us a little bit about that so we can round off that topic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our regulations, a soldier can refuse to carry out an order from his superior only on condition if that order would constitute an act which would be sanctioned under some law or which would constitute a criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already answered the Prosecutor about which orders the commander of the 17th Tactical Group issued, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. The first order was to mobilise the detachment. Do you hold that this was a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The second order that you received was to set up defensive lines in the outlying areas, on the outskirts of the town. Is that a criminal act, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The third order was issued to you about the collection of illegal military weapons from the citizens of Bosanski Samac. Is that, in your opinion and in your criteria, a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any order from the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, which would, according to what you know and understand, constitute a criminal act under the laws that were in force at the time? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: He's no legal expert, for a start, and he shouldn't be called upon to answer these questions. He's given clear evidence of the orders that he was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, actually, and it doesn't even help the defence of Mr. Zaric. MR. DI FAZIO: It's just irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Asking along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have just completed this line of questioning with this question, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor showed you or discussed with you the document of Biljana Plavsic, you answered a number of questions on that topic. I'm not quite sure, but I would like to ask you one question which is as follows: Did the Yugoslav People's Army or the 17th Tactical Group arm all the members of the 4th Detachment, regardless of their ethnic, religious, or political orientation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. It armed everybody, regardless of their ethnicity. It armed Serbs, Croats, and Muslims who were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You testified here in response to a question by my colleague Mr. Pantelic about filing criminal charges, and you said that that was not your responsibility. I wanted to ask you one question: Did you file criminal charges when you were physically mistreated by Lugar and other members of the paramilitary formation, i.e. those volunteers who had arrived, and what did you undertake at that moment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not file any criminal charges against Lugar, who beat me, mistreated me, arrested me, insulted me, maybe because I did not wish to enter into any deeper conflicts, but I did do what any man would do who values his dignity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I submitted a report to my superior commander, asked to be discharged of my duties, and I went to the trenches and continued as a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I just have one question for you, Mr. Antic. I think it would be most helpful to the Trial Chamber if you, as the commander of the 4th Detachment, 17th, 18th, and so on of April, until you handed in your resignation, if you could tell us: What was the role, if any, of Mr. Miroslav Tadic and Mr. Simo Zaric with respect to the collection of weapons in the town of Bosanski Samac; and secondly, whether there was a Praga or a tank involved in the collection of those weapons, if you know, as commander of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once I received the order from Commander Nikolic to implement this activity, I conveyed this order to my command, informed all of its members, and issued specific tasks, and that is also the monitoring of the implementation of that order. And I also, besides Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric, I participated in the implementation myself. The action, as I said before, was carried out without any incidents. There were no complaints from the citizens. They voluntarily brought out the weapons and handed them over. Mr. Tadic had the task of registering all the weapons and of handing over the weapons to the warehouse. Mr. Zaric, together with me, also had the task of monitoring the implementation of the order, in accordance with his responsibility, i.e., to come and intervene in the event of an incident which could occur while this was being carried out. I stress: These weapons, military weapons, were illegally possessed by Samac citizens. Whether any vehicle, an APC, took part in that, that is the question. I said that on the 17th, in the afternoon, two such vehicles turned up as a form of support in the implementation of the task of the 4th Detachment. I didn't understand that these vehicles were sent by the command of the 17th Tactical Group in order for this order to be carried out. However, at any point there was a danger that, from the direction of the village of Prud or from the direction of Croatia, some combat activities could be directed against the 4th Detachment and the town of Samac, and this really did happen, because firing broke out immediately. Over a period of four days, the town went through such horror. Everything was demolished. Not a single pane of glass was left whole on the buildings, on the shops. All the streets were filled with rubble, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. I think if we can go back to my question, though, Mr. Antic. I think well all understand that there was a lot of destruction from the shelling. But what I think would assist us to know, if you have any knowledge as to whether, in terms of collection of weapons, there was -- and whether we call it an APC, a Praga, a tank, was there a military vehicle of some nature that accompanied the persons from the 4th Detachment who were collecting the weapons and went from street to street? So if you could answer that first, and then I'll come back with a supplementary question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The function of these vehicles was not to collect weapons from the citizens, but, as I said, its role, its function, was completely different, which was to give support to the 4th Detachment because of the artillery fire which was happening at the time, and the 4th Detachment could not respond to this artillery fire. It was impossible to fight a combat against a tank, against a mortar, just with a rifle. And these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Antic. I think we're going off the point a little bit again. Could you just give me a direct answer. To your knowledge, as commander of the 4th Detachment and your subordinates were going out there, pursuant to orders, collecting weapons. Was there or was there not some type of armoured vehicle? I say whether it was an APC, a Praga, a tank. We won't worry about the distinctions of that. But was there or was there not such a type of vehicle going up and down the streets, stopping in front of people's houses or apartments, 4th Detachment people going in, collecting the weapons with this vehicle sitting on the street outside? If you know, please tell us; if you don't know, please tell us also.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I was the one who personally checked, and Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic, I can say that there was no such vehicle in my immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. And just the one follow-up question which is my only other question is, in terms of the role of Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic, did you, as the commander of the 4th Detachment, give them orders to go personally with the members of the 4th Detachment from apartment to apartment or house to house to see and to ask for weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, that I did issue them with such tasks, and I participated as well. But I'd like to make a correction. We did not enter apartments or even yards or houses, but we went down the street and called on citizens to take the weapons out. That was the strict order, and it was respected as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antic, for giving evidence to the Trial Chamber. We are finished now. You may leave the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we bring our next witness, can I just very briefly address to the Trial Chamber, because I have some concerns. If I could have only two minutes in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA SIMIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We'll start with your examination-in-chief now, but first I'd just like to remind you of the instructions that I gave you in relation to the speed of talking. If you can please wait a second when I finish my question and then answer, so that we don't have the overlap. That is for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, for the record, can you please tell us your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA SIMIC
utterances.text: Kosta Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA SIMIC
